regulations.title: French must be the dominant language on packaging (Charter of the French Language)
regulations.summary: Any writing on your product, container, or package must appear in French, and the French text has to be at least as prominent as any other language on the label. An English-only label, or a label where English is bigger or more visible than the French, is not allowed.
regulations.regulation_name: Charter of the French Language, s. 51, and the Regulation respecting the language of commerce and business
regulations.authority: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
regulations.action_required: Redesign packaging so French text is at least as prominent as any other language, covering product name, ingredient list, and claims.
regulations.penalty_note: OQLF can issue demand letters and pursue fines for non-compliant packaging; repeat offences escalate penalties.
regulations.source_name: Office québécois de la langue française

regulations.title: Trademarks and descriptive product terms must be translated (Bill 96 update)
regulations.summary: As of June 1, 2025, if your brand name or trademark includes non-French descriptive words (not just a registered trademark), those descriptive terms generally need a French translation on the packaging, with grace periods running to 2027 for existing stock.
regulations.regulation_name: Bill 96 (Act respecting French, the official and common language of Québec), amending the Charter of the French Language
regulations.authority: Office québécois de la langue française (OQLF)
regulations.action_required: Review product/brand names for descriptive English terms and add French translations to packaging before selling in Quebec.
regulations.penalty_note: Non-compliance is enforced the same way as other Charter labelling violations: demand letters, then fines.
regulations.source_name: Office québécois de la langue française

regulations.title: Retail/food preparation permit from MAPAQ
regulations.summary: Any business that prepares, packages, or sells food to the public in Quebec (including a bakery selling packaged baked goods) needs a permit from the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries and Food (MAPAQ) before opening, covering the specific category of food activity.
regulations.regulation_name: Food Products Act (Loi sur les produits alimentaires) and its regulations
regulations.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ)
regulations.action_required: Apply for a MAPAQ retail/food preparation permit for the applicable food category before selling any product in Quebec.
regulations.penalty_note: Operating without a required MAPAQ permit can result in fines and forced closure until compliant.

regulations.title: Mandatory food handler / food safety training
regulations.summary: At least one person responsible for food handling at your establishment must complete MAPAQ-recognized food safety (hygiene and sanitation) training before the permit is issued or shortly after opening.
regulations.regulation_name: Food Products Act - mandatory training requirement (Loi sur les produits alimentaires)
regulations.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ)
regulations.action_required: Enroll a designated staff member in a MAPAQ-recognized food safety training course and keep the certificate on file.
regulations.penalty_note: Missing training can delay or block permit issuance and lead to fines on inspection.

regulations.title: On-site MAPAQ inspection before and after opening
regulations.summary: MAPAQ inspectors verify that your kitchen or production facility meets sanitation and layout standards before issuing a permit, and can conduct unannounced follow-up inspections afterward.
regulations.authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ)
regulations.action_required: Prepare your production facility to meet MAPAQ sanitation standards and schedule the pre-opening inspection.
regulations.penalty_note: A failed inspection blocks permit issuance until deficiencies are corrected and re-inspected.

regulations.title: Quebec Sales Tax (QST) registration for taxable food sales
regulations.summary: Most packaged/prepared food sold in Quebec is taxable and requires the seller to register for and collect Quebec Sales Tax (QST), in addition to federal GST, once you have a physical or significant presence in the province.
regulations.regulation_name: Act respecting the Québec sales tax
regulations.action_required: Register for a QST number with Revenu Québec before making taxable sales in the province.
regulations.penalty_note: Selling without required QST registration can result in retroactive tax assessments and penalties.
